subject: CentronAI - SLA availability offsets and mitigations (order form redlines)
messages:
From: Samira Khan <samira.khan@centronai.com>
To: connor.obrien@redwood.inference.com
Cc: Amit Rao <amit.rao@centronai.com>, legal@centronai.com
Date: 2028-05-30T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: CentronAI redlines - SLA and availability

Connor —

Thanks again for the walkthrough yesterday. Attached is our team's redline of the Order Form and the SLA matrix (attachments: CentronAI_OrderForm_Redline_v3.pdf; SLA_Availability_Matrix.xlsx). Key asks from CentronAI Legal and Ops (high level):

- Uptime target: request firm 99.95% for production endpoints (we rely on single-region with active-active traffic shaping).
- Service credits: propose a linear credit schedule capped at 6 months' credit for extreme outages; we left specific percentages in the matrix.
- Response times: P1 acknowledge within 30 minutes and mitigation plan within 4 hours; P2 within 4 hours.
- Maintenance windows: restrict recurring maintenance to a 2-hour monthly window between 02:00–04:00 local time and require 7 days' notice. No routine maintenance permitted during blackout periods (quarterly release windows).

If Redwood cannot accept the 99.95% floor due to single-region constraints, we can discuss a multi-region premium or a different credit cap. We marked trade-offs inline. Can you route these to legal and ops and let us know Redwood's positions?

Best,
Samira Khan
Head of Infrastructure Programs
CentronAI

Attachments: CentronAI_OrderForm_Redline_v3.pdf (pdf, 158KB); SLA_Availability_Matrix.xlsx (spreadsheet, 47KB)

From: marissa_cole@redwood.inference.com
To: connor.obrien@redwood.inference.com, Samira Khan <samira.khan@centronai.com>
Cc: lauren_bishop@redwood.inference.com, karthik_iyer@redwood.inference.com
Date: 2028-05-30T14:26:00-07:00
Subject: RE: CentronAI redlines - SLA and availability

Samira / Connor —

Thanks — I reviewed the redline and matrix. Below are Redwood Legal/OPS positions and suggested language to add to the MSA/Order Form. I tried to keep the trade-offs explicit so procurement can align quickly.

1) Uptime target (availability metric)
- Position: Standard offering: 99.9% monthly for single-region deployments.
- Premium option: 99.95% monthly if customer elects the Availability Rider (additional monthly fee; auto-enables multi-region mirror or reserved warm-standby). We can offer 99.95% for single-region only if the customer accepts an availability rider and runbook obligations (failover test cadence, additional observability hooks).

Suggested clause: "Customer may elect the Availability Rider to increase the Service Uptime commitment to 99.95% for the Service Plan specified in the Order Form; such election requires the Availability Rider Fee and adherence to the Runbook and Failover Test Schedule attached as Exhibit A."

2) Service credits
- Position: Linear credit schedule tied to monthly uptime banding, capped at 3 months' recurring fees for standard plans. For customers who take the Availability Rider, cap increases to 6 months.

Suggested clause: "Service Credits shall be calculated per the SLA Matrix (Exhibit B) and the total aggregate credit for any 12-month period shall not exceed the lesser of three (3) months' Monthly Recurring Charges for the Service Plan, or, if Customer has elected the Availability Rider, six (6) months' MRC."

3) Response times (incident triage)
- Position: P1 (critical): initial response within 1 hour; P1 mitigation plan within 4 hours. P2: initial response within 4 hours; mitigation plan within 24 hours. Willing to accept a 30-minute initial ACK for P1 if customer purchases Premium Support add-on (adds on-call slack and dedicated contact).

4) Maintenance windows
- Position: We accept a monthly 2-hour maintenance window with 7 days' notice for routine maintenance. We cannot guarantee zero maintenance during your internal blackout periods but will agree to avoid scheduled maintenance in those windows where operationally possible and will provide a 72-hour exception for critical releases if mutually agreed. Emergency maintenance (security, critical stability) is excluded but will be notified ASAP; we will not perform emergency maintenance that introduces breaking behavior without prior coordination unless required.

5) Operational mitigations (non-contractual)
- We propose a warm-standby failover architecture with documented RTO/RPO in Exhibit A. This reduces likelihood of credits and is included in Availability Rider options.

Next steps: I can prepare a redline counter-proposal that inserts the Availability Rider and the two-tier credit caps, plus an option row in the Order Form for Premium Support. If CentronAI wants 99.95 without the rider, we will need legal escalation and an underwriting review (possible security / capacity covenants).

Please let me know which path you prefer and whether CentronAI will consider the Availability Rider / Premium Support trade-off. If agreeable, I will send a tracked redline for the Order Form and an updated SLA matrix.

—
Marissa Cole
Senior Counsel, Contracts & Commercial
Redwood Inference
marissa_cole@redwood.inference.com

(Attachment note: drafting summary only; formal redline to follow)

From: Amit Rao <amit.rao@centronai.com>
To: marissa_cole@redwood.inference.com, connor.obrien@redwood.inference.com
Cc: Samira Khan <samira.khan@centronai.com>, legal@centronai.com
Date: 2028-05-31T08:57:00-07:00
Subject: RE: CentronAI redlines - SLA and availability

Marissa / team —

Thanks for the quick and concrete options. A few points from our side after internal review:

- CentronAI is willing to accept the Availability Rider model, provided the rider can be executed within 30 days of signing and the cost is clearly stated in the Order Form. We prefer the 99.95% floor for production; the rider + fee approach is acceptable so long as the rider comes with the warm-standby implementation plan (Exhibit A) and a quarterly failover test commitment.
- On credits: we can accept a 3-month cap for standard but maintain that for production-critical endpoints covered by the Availability Rider the cap should be 6 months (your suggestion aligns).
- Response times: 30-minute P1 ACK is important to us. We are open to Premium Support if you can quantify the monthly fee. Please include a clear opt-in checkbox in the Order Form.
- Maintenance windows: 7 days' notice works. We need explicit language that Redwood will not schedule routine maintenance during the customer blackout weeks (we will provide dates at contract signature). If emergency maintenance is required, we ask for post-event RCA within 48 hours.

I've attached a lightly edited redline showing acceptance of the rider approach and with a note to include pricing for Premium Support (attachment: CentronAI_OrderForm_Redline_v3_ami_updated.pdf).

Can Marissa / legal produce the final tracked redline and draft Availability Rider pricing options? We want to close by EOW if possible — our procurement cycle is tight.

Best,
Amit Rao
Head of Procurement, CentronAI

Attachments: CentronAI_OrderForm_Redline_v3_ami_updated.pdf (pdf, 162KB)
